answer: Divergent-State Handshake. Each identity must maintain a private state quill that evolves from its own transaction history. To act on the wharf, an agent signs a challenge binding its current state root. Clones share identical histories, so they produce identical roots and collide on the same challenge, exposing the fork. Honest agents diverge because their local lagoon of interactions differs. An attacker must run each clone through unique activity, paying full per-identity compute and latency costs to force divergence, making N clones cost N times the real work.
